clue.text: Court puts HM in dodgy situation

indicators.note: the word for Her Majesty is placed in the middle of the word meaning dodgy

parts.note: dodgy means risky, chancy
HM is Her Majesty, ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: A court case lands the monarch in an awkward predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts' is only a link. ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the usual crossword shorthand for the monarch, and 'Court' is the definition, not a royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Court of Chancery is a division of the English High Court of Justice.

clue.text: A student festival being staged in Spain

parts.note: rag week is a British student fundraising festival
a play being staged is on

explanation.surface: A college rag week is put on somewhere in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG is a British student charity festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Aragon is a historic region and autonomous community of north-east Spain.

clue.text: Isolated after being disinherited

explanation.surface: Someone left alone once removed from the will.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a remote place is separated from others, and an heir cut off loses an inheritance.

clue.text: Red-headed courtesan made them tell tales

definitions.note: read as those who tell tales, a noun for people

parts.note: the head of the word red is its first letter

indicators.note: made is read as made into something new, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A scarlet-haired courtesan got her clients gossiping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red-headed' gives R, the first letter of 'red'; 'made' shuffles R plus COURTESAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Storytellers who entertain with anecdotes are called raconteurs.

clue.text: Small dessert made with common vegetable

parts.note: pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: A little pudding made with an everyday vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is slang for a potato, the commonest vegetable.

clue.text: Arrested after having stopped in a lay-by

explanation.surface: A driver who parked in a roadside stop got nicked.
explanation.walkthrough: A lay-by is a British roadside parking bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Police pull in a suspect when they detain them; a driver pulls in to stop at the roadside.

clue.text: Ditch fish and pastry pudding

parts.note: to ditch is to dump
a ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Throw away the fish and the stodgy pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple dumpling is a sweet baked in pastry, a classic pudding.

clue.text: Opening for a saucy northern banker

parts.note: saucy means cheeky, pert
a banker is something with banks, a river; the Ure is a river in northern England

explanation.surface: A cheeky northern bank clerk gets a job opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a crossword trick for a river; the Ure flows through Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a gap or hole, as in a camera lens.

clue.text: Proceed to enter charge, as is the custom

indicators.note: one word goes into the other, entering it

parts.note: a charge is the price asked
to proceed is to act, take action

explanation.surface: Go ahead and add the fee, as is usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice is an habitual way of doing things, a custom.

clue.text: In Aleppo shoes are stylish

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words Aleppo shoes

explanation.surface: Footwear in the Syrian city of Aleppo is fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh means smart or upmarket, hence stylish.

clue.text: Way to cook meat in iron container

indicators.note: the meat is put in the iron container

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: Cooking meat in a cast-iron pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To flambé is to cook food doused in burning spirit.

clue.text: What a gourmand likes is making gibes

explanation.surface: A greedy eater also enjoys mocking people.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoffing means eating greedily, beloved of a glutton, and also jeering or mocking.

clue.text: Fanatic unknown to each group

parts.note: in algebra unknowns are x, y and z
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A fanatic is a stranger to every faction.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is an extreme, uncompromising enthusiast.

clue.text: Initially the clear leader

explanation.surface: From the start, out in front by a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to begin with, and literally names whoever is ahead of everyone.

clue.text: Supplicant given order to peer into it

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A humble applicant is told to look into the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the anagram is of PEER INTO IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A petitioner is someone who formally asks or begs, a supplicant.

clue.text: Civil service upset by one article that's vitriolic

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, so backwards

parts.note: one gives a, the indefinite article
an article is an item, a thing

explanation.surface: Civil servants are angered by a newspaper piece that's poisonous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like the grammar word for A, but here it is THING; 'one' is A.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathing criticism is bitterly severe, like acid.

clue.text: Wonderful potato dish carol consumed

indicators.note: the potato dish is swallowed up by the carol, sitting inside it

parts.note: to carol is to sing
mash is mashed potato

explanation.surface: Lovely mashed potato eaten by a woman called Carol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carol' looks like a name; it is the verb, to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is British slang for excellent or terrific.

clue.text: Mae truly went west in sophisticated style

indicators.note: went west means was ruined or collapsed, so the letters fall apart and regroup

explanation.surface: Mae West truly behaved in a worldly fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Mae West was a famously suggestive film star; 'went west' signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting maturely means behaving in a grown-up, refined way.

clue.text: Happen to discover how to make an impression

explanation.surface: Advice on chancing upon something and seeming impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across is to find by chance; it also means to appear or seem to others.

clue.text: Enthralled when house was approved?

parts.note: OK'd means given approval

explanation.surface: Captivated at the moment the building plans got passed.
explanation.walkthrough: OK'ED is OK used as a verb, written without the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooked means captivated or addicted.

clue.text: Indian savoury pole found in Pacific archipelago

indicators.note: the pole is located inside the island name

parts.note: Samoa is an island group in the South Pacific
S is the South Pole

explanation.surface: A spicy snack and a mast discovered on Pacific islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried pastry with a spiced filling from South Asia.

clue.text: Scheme to get allotment

explanation.surface: A plan to acquire a garden patch.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a British rented vegetable plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret plan, and also a small piece of land.

clue.text: 50-50 chance that dipso reverts to drink

indicators.note: reverts means goes back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a dipso (dipsomaniac) is a sot, a drunkard
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Even odds that the alcoholic falls off the wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A toss-up is an even chance, like flipping a coin.

clue.text: One track for which Maureen gets no censure

parts.note: Mo is short for Maureen
to rail is to complain bitterly, censure

explanation.surface: Maureen escapes blame for her single-minded attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One track' looks like one-track mind; it is a single rail.
explanation.definitionFit: A monorail runs on one rail, a single track.

clue.text: Is about to get up, then flags

indicators.note: about means around, so the word is wrapped round the other

parts.note: to get up is to rise

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to get out of bed, then tires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flags' looks like a verb meaning tires; it is the plant (yellow flag iris).
explanation.definitionFit: The flag is a common name for the wild iris plant.

clue.text: Behave brutally, getting John the sack

parts.note: Jack is a familiar form of John
getting the sack is getting the boot

explanation.surface: John turns nasty on being dismissed from his job.
explanation.definitionFit: To jackboot is to act in an oppressive, bullying way, from military boots.

clue.text: Non-Jew confronts a Spanish painter

parts.note: goy is a Yiddish word for a gentile

explanation.surface: A gentile faces a Spanish artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a celebrated Spanish painter.

clue.text: Laggards turned out in best bib and tucker

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters are tipped out and rearranged

explanation.surface: Latecomers arrive in their finest clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best bib and tucker' is an old idiom for one's smartest clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is slang for party clothes, one's finery.
